name: Falconer distance-set conjecture
question: Does Hausdorff dimension greater than d/2 imply positive Lebesgue measure of its distance set?
first_attack: Audit precise statement and prove a restricted case
method_title: One set, dimension and measure enclosed
dispatch_next: Audit FalconerAllDimensions.lean definition fidelity, measure conventions and proof dependencies; obtain independent harmonic-analysis review.
dispatch_why: A manuscript may already settle this entry. The next step is the review's own check, not a new lemma.

claim_review_2026.primary_title: The Falconer distance conjecture in all dimensions
claim_review_2026.claimed_theorem: For every integer d>=2 and compact E subset R^d with Hausdorff dimension greater than d/2, the Euclidean distance set Delta(E) has positive one-dimensional Lebesgue measure.
claim_review_2026.scope_note: The strict threshold and positive-measure conclusion match the registered Falconer formulation; no endpoint equality or pinned-distance result is claimed.
claim_review_2026.known_caveats: The repository describes Lean theorem scope, but a stated source/Lean match has not been established by two independent specialist proof audits.
claim_review_2026.next_review: Audit FalconerAllDimensions.lean definition fidelity, measure conventions and proof dependencies; obtain independent harmonic-analysis review.
